item.subject: maths
item.stem: The diagram shows Ekta's algebra grid. One row has three identical green squares with sum $15$. The next row has two identical yellow circles and one green square with sum $17$. Each shape stands for one unknown value.

parts.text: Which claim correctly finds the shape values?

options.text: From three green squares summing to $15$, one green square is $5$. Then two yellow circles and one green square summing to $17$ give one yellow circle equal to $6$.
Call each shape an unknown and stop, leaving the sums $15$ and $17$ unused.
Factorise $15$ and $17$ into primes and treat those factors as the shape values.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.
